assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a general, predictable bond-forming reaction. Ligand design, from early bidentate phosphines to bulky electron-rich biaryl and ferrocenyl ligands, made it broadly usable; it is now routine in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Originality is high and the chemical clarity is exceptional, though it builds on the already recognized 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic methodology and the ligand architectures independently and in parallel, with mechanistic work by both. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor but not the general catalytic amination, so a two-person prize looks fair. Credit for individual ligand generations could be debated.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of use, thousands of independent applications, industrial scale-up and complete mechanistic understanding. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Committee may feel the 2010 cross-coupling prize already covers the field.
Kosugi's precursor role and the relative weighting of ligand design versus the reaction itself are not resolved from the supplied text.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the history, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell reactivity under mild conditions with simple catalysts and light, enabling new disconnections and late-stage functionalization. It is conceptually fresh, widely adopted in medicinal and process chemistry, and changed how synthetic chemists plan bond formation.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently reported the organic-synthesis use of Ru and Ir polypyridyl and organic photocatalysts around 2008-2011, alongside MacMillan, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021) for a different discovery; I leave him out so the prize rewards the field's origin without duplicating his recognition. Which trio is fairest is contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and broadly adopted in industry and academia, with continuing mechanistic refinement. Mature enough, though the field is still changing quickly.
uncertainties: Priority among early contributors, including the Konig and Fukuzumi precedents, is contested.
MacMillan's central role could make a prize without him look incomplete.
The mechanistic picture, chain versus non-chain processes, differs across reaction classes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality, event-driven removal of proteins rather than occupancy-based inhibition. The chemistry (heterobifunctional design, ligand-E3 recruitment, glue mechanisms) is original, and clinical candidates are now in late-stage trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first implemented PROTACs; Ciulli made the VHL ligand and structural basis that made the technology rational. The thalidomide-glue story (Handa, Ito and others) is a separate strand with distinct credit. With up to eight names, a three-person prize requires hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic and preclinical confirmation is strong, but no PROTAC drug has been fully approved yet, so the long-term impact is still being established.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete, so recognition may be premature.
The PROTAC and molecular-glue strands may need separate recognition.
Credit among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Gray and the thalidomide researchers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization with ligand and template control converted ubiquitous C-H bonds into selective sites for synthesis, shortening routes to complex molecules in line with step economy. Yu's ligand-enabled and distal-selective methods, Hartwig's borylation and Sanford's high-valent Pd chemistry are conceptually and practically important.
assessment.attribution: Yu, Hartwig and Sanford each made decisive, distinct contributions. Daugulis and Smith are credited for early directed and borylation work. Credit is spread across several independent lines, which complicates configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely used in synthesis and industrial settings, with strong independent confirmation, though predictability and scope are still evolving.
uncertainties: Several distinct subfields (directed Pd, borylation, undirected) are bundled together.
Whether the core idea is mature enough as a general synthetic tool, and the relative weight of early work by Murai and others not credited here, remain unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors enable single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks, with Liu's directed evolution of deaminases built on CRISPR proteins. The work is chemically sophisticated and has enormous therapeutic and research impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering effort; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead scientists of the cytosine and adenine editors. Giving the prize to Liu alone, or Liu with the trainees, is a likely debate. The CRISPR itself was recognized in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are underway and the approach is replicated across many labs, but human therapeutic outcomes are still early.
uncertainties: Whether this is chemistry versus biology or medicine, and how much of it rests on the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Allocation between Liu and trainees, and Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine deaminase editing, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide segments, making total chemical synthesis of proteins practical, and expressed protein ligation extended it to semisynthesis. It is a lasting, clean chemical invention that gave access to precisely modified proteins.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed native chemical ligation with Muir and Dawson in the first expressed-protein-ligation work; Danishefsky contributed to ligation-desulfurization strategies. Kent, Dawson and Muir is a reasonable core trio, but Brik, Liu and Danishefsky are also credited for extensions.
assessment.maturity: Established for over twenty-five years with broad independent use, though the therapeutic and wider scientific impact is narrower than for some other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the impact is broad enough compared with other candidates.
Division of credit between the original ligation and later extensions such as desulfurization is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allows site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids in living cells, creating a new chemistry of proteins in vivo. It is original and widely used, from bioorthogonal labelling to engineered proteins.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the general approach in bacteria, yeast and mammalian cells. Chin extended it to quadruplet codons, orthogonal ribosomes and multicellular organisms. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama also made substantive contributions, so a two- or three-person split needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated in many labs, though practical applications are still mostly in research tools and protein engineering rather than major products.
uncertainties: Credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is shared and contestable.
Overlap with the 2018 directed evolution prize and the ties to biology may affect the committee view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered Lewis acids and bases can heterolytically activate H2 and other small molecules without a transition metal, a conceptual shift in main-group reactivity with applications in metal-free hydrogenation and catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan reported the first metal-free reversible H2 activation in 2006, and Erker's group provided key contemporaneous and subsequent work, so a Stephan and Erker prize seems fair. Others in the field such as Tamm and Wass are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and expanded, but practical catalysis is still limited compared with transition-metal hydrogenation, so the long-term importance is not settled.
uncertainties: Practical impact versus conceptual novelty is not yet clear.
The early priority and scope relative to the Power and Bertrand work on main-group activation is debated, and I have not verified details.
